ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the energy bands are labeled from top to bottom as Vacuum level, Ec, Ei, EFs, Ev. The energy difference from the vacuum level to the conduction band bottom Ec is labeled as 4 eV, therefore the electron affinity chi = 4 eV. In the figure, the difference from Ec to Ei is 0.5 eV; EFs is located 0.2 eV above Ev. Since the bandgap is 1 eV, Ei is located in the middle of the bandgap, so Ei - Ev = 0.5 eV, therefore Ei - EFs = 0.5 - 0.2 = 0.3 eV. Reasoning calculation: Ec - EF = (Ec - Ei) + (Ei - EF) = 0.5 + 0.3 = 0.8 eV. The semiconductor work function phi_s = chi + (Ec - EF) = 4 + 0.8 = 4.8 eV. The metal work function is phi_m = 3.87 eV, and there is no charge in the oxide layer, so the flat-band voltage V_FB = phi_m - phi_s = 3.87 - 4.8 = -0.93 V. From the Fermi-potential-related energy difference in the figure, 2phi_F = 2(Ei - EF) = 0.6 V. According to the given threshold relationship V_TH = V_FB + 2phi_F + |Q_dep|/Cox', substitute V_TH = -0.16 V, V_FB = -0.93 V, Cox' = 100 nF/cm^2 = 1.0e-7 F/cm^2: |Q_dep|/Cox' = -0.16 - (-0.93) - 0.6 = 0.17 V. Therefore |Q_dep| = 0.17 × 1.0e-7 = 1.7e-8 C/cm^2.

raw_record.question_text: The band diagram of a p-type semiconductor with a band-gap of 1 eV is shown. Then compute phi_s = 4 + 0.8 = 4.8 eV and V_FB = phi_m - phi_s = 3.87 - 4.8 = -0.93 V. Use the text-given V_TH = -0.16 V and Cox' = 100 nF/cm^2 = 1.0e-7 F/cm^2. Insert into V_TH = V_FB + 2phi_F + |Q_dep|/Cox', with 2phi_F = 0.6 V, giving |Q_dep|/Cox' = -0.16 - (-0.93) - 0.6 = 0.17 V. Multiply by Cox' to obtain |Q_dep| = 1.7e-8 C/cm^2.

According to the given threshold relationship V_TH = V_FB + 2phi_F + |Q_dep|/Cox', substitute V_TH = -0.16 V, V_FB = -0.93 V, Cox' = 100 nF/cm^2 = 1.0e-7 F/cm^2: |Q_dep|/Cox' = -0.16 - (-0.93) - 0.6 = 0.17 V. Therefore |Q_dep| = 0.17 × 1.0e-7 = 1.7e-8 C/cm^2.
